title: A patchy reference screen permits 14 tested ice laws in the 2022 Gaia20cdd three-band depth test
abstract: We test an obscured reference state in the published 2022 Gaia20cdd g, r and W1 depth summaries. Positive column distributions in both states permit all 14 selected ice laws. The minimum hidden reference r attenuation is 0.6601-1.7456 mag when columns can rise or fall. Feasible solutions and continuous dual bounds bracket each minimum within 0.000130 mag. If dust can only be added on each ray, grid solutions need 1.5787-3.3093 mag. One added-dust witness hides 1.58 mag in r but changes g-r by only 0.097 mag. A uniform persistent screen cannot give this escape. A fixed permissive depth sensitivity lowers the free-column range to 0.1403-0.8401 mag. These are conditional model tests, not ice detections or confidence intervals. Limits include nonsimultaneous depths, fixed effective band opacities, equal source weights, a finite grain family, no emitted light, and only three bands. Code, witnesses, numerical bounds and source hashes are included.

display.caption: Hidden reference r attenuation for 14 selected ice laws. Free-column minima have continuous dual bounds. Added-dust points are feasible grid solutions. The depth sensitivity is a fixed tolerance test, not a confidence region.
